questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a German-speaking country and to a larger city, because I wanted to connect with people fast. Therefore I considered Vienna a cool opportunity - also getting to know Austria!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The international office of the university was always ready to help. I stayed in a WG with other students, who could help me, so I didn´t need much information from the office - but I´m sure, they are always ready to help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn´t get any help from the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It took me a couple of weeks - I used wg-gesucht!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was the best experience - I also lived in a wg in Germany a couple weeks ago and this time was just as amazing

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found a very nice WG on WG-gesucht! Can definitely recommend trying to find something on your own.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I went to the International Office to pick up a document - there were a lot of time slots and it was very easy and convenient.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don´t know, since I didn´t ask for help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the classes, that I wanted to take. Dont forget the rating - the system with the 1000 points, with which you can be sure to get at least some of the courses you want to take!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Its´s not at all complicated! Just read your emails and go pick up the document. And ask for help if you have any questions!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It differed a lot. I took 2 Pro-Seminar Course, which were very good and one Einführung in die Literaturwissenschaft Course, which was less challenging, but also because it was really just an introduction.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I think it was not so different from KU. It of course differed according to the professor, but I learnt a lot. And I can definitely recommend the Proseminar Course, which is always offered in the Spring Semester (if you study literature) with an excursion to the Rauriser Literaturtage - it was a very nice opportunity to get to know other students better and see other areas of Austria. Generally, look out for the courses with included excursion!

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Proseminar NdL: Literarische Neuerscheinungen
Einführung in die Literaturwissenschaft: Wiener Moderne
VO: Die anderen in mir – zur literarischen Selbstgestaltung von Selbst- und Fremderlebnissen
VO: Gegenwartsliteratur
NDL: Theorien des literarischen Lesens
Proseminar: Literatur zur Sprache bringen: Literarische Gespräche im Unterricht

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Konversatorium NDL: Theorien des literarischen Lesens
Proseminar: Literatur zur Sprache bringen: Literarische Gespräche im Unterricht
VO: Gegenwartsliteratur
Proseminar NdL: Literarische Neuerscheinungen

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn´t encounter any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The USI (Uni Sport Courses) were not as expensive as I thought, so I signed up for a couple of courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: USI-courses are very nice. Maybe consider which courses you take, if you want to connect with people. Zumba wasn´t the best choice. Be aware of the registration date and wake up early if you for instance wants to play beach volleyball - was completely booked out after a couple of minutes.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a free concert with Musik Verein in the Arkadenhof. I also went on two excursions with the courses I signed up for - the university payed for transport and hotel and it was a very interesting, cultural experience. I went to Burgtheater a couple of times, because you only pay 10 euros as a student. The erasmus-team was also very kind and answered so many questions in the group chat.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Burgtheater - generally going in the theater, tickets are very cheap for students. I also went to Musik Verein and bought a membership to a couple of museums, because it already after the second visit was cheaper. During summer the festival season is so crazy - so many events and concerts for free in the city. I also went to a couple of readings with various authors - also a very nice kind of event, if you´re interested in literature.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went to Budapest, Bratislava, Brno, Graz, Klagenfurt and Innsbruck. And went hiking at the Schneeberg, went to visit a couple of "Heurigen" at Kahlenberg.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the courses with excursions!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Vienna has culturally so much to offer! And the people I met at university were also very friendly and open-minded!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the beautiful sorroundings - both the university and the city! It was in the beginning very overwhelming, but I slowly got used to studying in what would have been worthy of housing some monarch! Pick some of the courses with excursion and find a WG where you can get to know locals!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Even though you have a lot of small courses or at least courses which only give you 3-4 ECTS points and it can be hard to keep track of the many courses, it will be all right in the end. Maybe if possible start writing some of your papers so that you can also enjoy the summer outside of the reading rooms (MAK has a good one! you can enter for free)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Improving my german skills and getting to know very nice and kind people - and experiencing that my work payed of and I managed to get through all of my courses - even though it was hard to keep track in the beginning!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The many (6) courses, because we rather have to larger courses in Copenhagen.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
